title: Count Operations to Obtain Zero
summary: Given two non-negative integers, repeatedly subtract the smaller number from the larger in one operation until one of the numbers becomes zero.
statement: Given two non-negative integers, repeatedly subtract the smaller number from the larger in one operation until one of the numbers becomes zero. The task is to determine the total number of such operations needed.
constraints: Each operation subtracts the smaller positive value from the larger, or num2 from num1 when equal.
Stop when either value reaches zero and return the number of individual subtractions.
hints: Repeated subtraction is the Euclidean algorithm with a count.
A quotient tells how many consecutive subtractions occur before the larger remainder becomes smaller.
While both are positive, add larger//smaller and replace the larger with its remainder.
Division groups exactly the same repeated subtractions without skipping the final subtraction that can produce zero.
editorial: Division groups exactly the same repeated subtractions without skipping the final subtraction that can produce zero.

tests.explanation: The states are (2,3), (2,1), (1,1), and (0,1), requiring three operations.
One subtraction changes the pair to (0,10), so return 1.
